q: I ___ to Cartagena three times, and I would love to go again.
e: Life experience with no finished time: present perfect.

q: We ___ the report last Friday.
e: 'Last Friday' is a finished time: past simple.

q: She ___ in Bogotá since 2015.
e: 'Since' + a state that continues now: present perfect.

q: When ___ your degree?
e: 'When' asks about a finished moment: past simple.

q: The number of cyclists ___ sharply over the past decade.
e: 'Over the past decade' reaches the present: present perfect.

q: In 2010, the company ___ 200 people.
e: A finished year: past simple.

q: I can't go out. I ___ my homework yet.
e: 'Yet' with a present result: present perfect.

q: How long ___ (you / know) your best friend?
e: 'How long' up to now: present perfect. 'Know' is a state verb, so no -ing.

q: My grandfather ___ (die) ten years ago.
e: 'Ago' always takes the past simple.

q: This is the best book I ___ (ever / read).
e: Superlative + ever: present perfect.

q: Unemployment ___ (fall) by 2% between 2015 and 2018.
e: A finished period in the past: past simple.

q: I ___ (work) here for six months, and I still love it.
e: Started in the past and continues: present perfect (simple or continuous).

q: She ___ (just / send) the email, so check your inbox.
e: 'Just' + a present result: present perfect.

q: I have visited my cousins last weekend.
fix: I visited my cousins last weekend.
e: 'Last weekend' is finished, so past simple.

q: She works in this company since January.
fix: She has worked in this company since January.
e: 'Since' needs the present perfect, not the present simple.

q: I know Maria since we were children.
fix: I have known Maria since we were children.
e: Conozco a María desde... → I have known.

q: Scientists have discovered penicillin in 1928.
e: A date makes the time finished: past simple.

q: I started studying English in 2020, and I still study it.
a: I have been studying English since 2020.
e: Present perfect + since + starting point.

q: The last time I saw her was in March.
a: I haven't seen her since March.
e: Negative present perfect + since.

q: He moved to Spain three years ago and he still lives there.
a: He has lived in Spain for three years.
He has been living in Spain for three years.
e: Present perfect + for + length of time.
